title: Udon Thani With Kids 2-3 Days — Ducks, Red Lotus, Ban Chiang | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A family-friendly Udon Thani itinerary in Thailand: play by the giant ducks at Nong Prajak, boat across the Red Lotus Sea, explore the Ban Chiang World Heritage site, plus kid cafes and timing that keeps toddlers happy.
keywords: Udon Thani with kids, Udon Thani family trip, Nong Prajak ducks, Red Lotus Sea, Ban Chiang
h1:
Udon With Kids
Ducks, Red Lotus, Ban Chiang
intro: Udon Thani is easier to do with kids than you'd think. The in-town sights are close together, there's a big park for them to run around, a World Heritage site to learn at, and a Red Lotus Sea where the boat ride gets them excited. We've put together a 2-3 day plan that keeps the driving light, paces the day around little ones so nobody has to wake up at dawn cranky, and works in a recharge stop at every turn.

blocks.html: Taking kids on a road trip, the thing you fear most is them getting bored mid-journey, hot, hungry and whiny. Udon Thani handles this well because the main sights aren't far apart. In town, Nong Prajak is a central park where kids can run and pose with the giant rubber ducks, while out-of-town trips like the Red Lotus Sea and Ban Chiang are only about an hour's drive away. We've designed each day around just one or two main activities, leaving plenty of time to rest, eat and squeeze in an afternoon nap.

blocks.title: Read before you plan
blocks.html: The Red Lotus Sea is seasonal. The lotus only blooms beautifully from early December to early March, and you have to go early (roughly 6am to 11am). If you come any other time of year, skip the lotus day and do the city plus Ban Chiang instead, and save the Red Lotus Sea for next trip.

Many families have just arrived on day one and the kids are still worn out from the car or plane, so you don't want to pack in heavy activities. We start with some warm food, then let the kids run loose at Nong Prajak, and wrap up with an easy stroll through the evening market.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: In-town Udon — Nong Prajak + UD Town

items.activity: Check in at a hotel in the town center, drop your bags and head out for a late breakfast
items.note: Pick a place near Nong Prajak or close to UD Town so you can walk to several spots

items.activity: Noodles at a beef-and-fish bowl shop on Chaloem Phrakiat Road near Nong Prajak
items.note: Airy, comfortable shop with a rich broth, easy noodles for kids. From 50-70 THB a bowl

items.activity: Back to the hotel for the kids' afternoon nap, dodging the hottest part of the day
items.note: Early afternoon in Isan, the sun is fierce — better to rest in the air-con than push through

items.activity: Nong Prajak Park — photos with the giant ducks, cycling, and let the kids loose on the playground
items.note: Free entry, with bikes and pedal cars for rent. The evening breeze makes it easy to walk a loop around the lake

items.activity: Stroll around UD Town in the center, have dinner, let the kids pick their own food
items.note: Lots of restaurants, an open-air seating zone, and live music and events at certain times

blocks.title: About the ducks
blocks.html: The giant rubber ducks at Nong Prajak are a favorite with kids, but the city sometimes takes them out for repairs or swaps them around for festivals (such as Songkran). If you're coming specifically to photograph the ducks, check the Udon Thani City Municipality page before you set off.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Red Lotus Sea boat ride (in season)

blocks.html: The highlight of the trip for kids is the boat ride out across a sea of pinkish-red lotus filling Nong Han Kumphawapi. Most kids get more excited about the boat than the flowers themselves, but the whole scene is pretty enough that the grown-ups will be snapping away too. The key thing is to go early, because the lotus closes up once the sun gets strong.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Red Lotus Sea, Kumphawapi (~45 km from town)

items.activity: Leave town heading for Kumphawapi district; pack snacks and water for the kids to have in the car
items.note: About a 45-60 min drive. You can use the Ban Diam or Ban Chaelae pier

items.activity: Board a boat to see the Red Lotus Sea — pick a small or large boat depending on family size
items.note: A small boat seats 2 for about 300 THB; a large boat seats around 6 for about 500 THB and takes roughly 1-1.5 hrs. Put a life jacket on every child

items.activity: Back on shore, breakfast near the pier with simple local food
items.note: The sun isn't strong yet at this point and the kids are still fresh

items.activity: Drive back into town, stopping at a kid cafe to escape the heat
items.note: Little Duck Kids Cafe or Kidkit Cafe have a play area and kids' menu items like fries, spaghetti and nuggets

items.activity: Lunch in town, then back for an afternoon nap
items.note: After a 5am start, the kids need to recharge in the afternoon

items.activity: Thai-Chinese Cultural Park (Pu-Ya Shrine), where the kids can feed the koi in the pond
items.note: A beautifully decorated Chinese garden with big koi in the pond. Kids love feeding the fish. Free entry

blocks.title: Boats and little ones
blocks.html: The Red Lotus Sea boats are open longtail boats, so very young children should be held and seated in the middle of the boat with a life jacket on the whole time. Bring hats, sunglasses and sunscreen, because the glare off the water is strong. If a child is scared of the boat, the lotus still looks lovely from the pier and the wooden walkway — no need to force the boat ride.

blocks.text: Day 3 — Ban Chiang World Heritage site

blocks.html: On the last day, take the kids for some fun learning at the Ban Chiang National Museum in Nong Han district, an archaeological site that was listed as a World Heritage site back in 1992. Kids get to see the real painted pots that are thousands of years old, plus the excavation pit at Wat Pho Si Nai where skeletons and vessels lie in the actual soil layers.

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: Ban Chiang, Nong Han district (~55 km from town)

items.activity: Leave town for Ban Chiang, about a 1-hour drive
items.note: The museum is open 09:00-16:00. Going early means an easier, cooler walk

items.activity: Walk through the Ban Chiang National Museum — painted pottery and bronze tools
items.note: Entry for Thais is in the tens of baht and uniformed students enter free. The building is air-conditioned, so you can take your time

items.activity: Walk over to the Wat Pho Si Nai excavation pit to see the real archaeological soil layers
items.note: It's near the museum, walkable. This is the spot kids get excited about because they see an actual dig

items.activity: Lunch in the Ban Chiang community, then browse the shops selling Ban Chiang patterned pottery souvenirs
items.note: There are Ban Chiang patterned keepsakes for the kids to pick out as a souvenir

items.activity: Drive back into town, stopping at a cafe by Nong Prajak to end the trip
items.note: Beyond Cafe's Nong Prajak branch is a big, airy waterside spot with homemade cakes and bakery items

blocks.text: Backup in-town spots in case the kids get bored

blocks.html: If the kids aren't ready to head home, or you hit a rainy day, there are spots right in town that they can enjoy without burning energy on travel. Keep these on hand to swap into the main plan.

items.name: Udon Thani Museum
items.blurb: Housed in the old Ratchinuthit building, with 26 rooms telling the story of Udon from its geology to its way of life. Air-conditioned, free entry, great for a rainy day.

items.name: Thai-Chinese Cultural Park (Pu-Ya Shrine)
items.blurb: A beautifully decorated Chinese garden with big koi for the kids to feed, lovely for photos and an easy evening stroll.

items.name: UD Town
items.blurb: A central shopping complex next to the train station, with an events plaza, restaurants and an evening market. Easy for kids to walk around, with convenient parking.

items.name: Kid cafes (Little Duck / Kidkit)
items.blurb: Cafes with play areas, both indoor air-con and outdoor, a full kids' menu, and somewhere for parents to sip coffee while the kids play for ages.

blocks.text: Tips for surviving Udon with kids

items: Rent a car and drive yourself — by far the easiest for families, since the Red Lotus Sea and Ban Chiang are out of town and public transport isn't great with little kids.
Put the lotus day early in the trip so you can shuffle days if the weather turns, and since you have to be up at 5am, get to bed early the night before.
Always keep snacks and water in the car. Hungry kids get whiny fast, especially on the lotus day when you leave before the shops open.
Avoid sightseeing in the early afternoon. Isan sun is strong and hot — use the afternoon for the kids to nap in the air-con and head out again in the evening.
Life jackets are a must the whole time you're on the lotus boat, and hold little ones in the middle of the boat.

faq.q: How many days are enough for a family trip to Udon Thani?
faq.a: 2-3 days is about right. Day one, take it easy around town at Nong Prajak and UD Town; day two, head to the Red Lotus Sea (December to March); day three, visit Ban Chiang. If you come outside the lotus season, two days is enough to cover the city and Ban Chiang.

faq.q: When can you visit the Red Lotus Sea and how much is the boat?
faq.a: The lotus blooms beautifully from early December to early March, and you should go early, around 6am to 11am, because the lotus closes up once the sun is strong. A small boat seats 2 for about 300 THB; a large boat seats around 6 for about 500 THB; the ride takes roughly 1-1.5 hours. Prices may vary by pier.

faq.q: Is Ban Chiang good for kids, or will they get bored?
faq.a: It's good. Beyond the air-conditioned museum, there's the Wat Pho Si Nai excavation pit where kids see skeletons and vessels in the actual soil layers. Most kids get excited about a real dig. You'll spend roughly 1-2 hours walking around — not too long.

faq.q: Are there places for little kids to play in town?
faq.a: Yes. Nong Prajak has a playground and bikes to rent. There are also kid cafes like Little Duck Kids Cafe and Kidkit Cafe with play areas and kids' menus, plus the Thai-Chinese Cultural Park where kids can feed the koi.

faq.q: Should we rent a car or use public transport when traveling with kids?
faq.a: Renting a car and driving yourself is far more convenient for families, since the Red Lotus Sea (about 45 km away) and Ban Chiang (about 55 km away) are out of town, and getting there by public transport with little kids and luggage is a hassle. In town, the main sights already have parking.
